entries.topic: The 1949 armistice lines, what the agreements said about borders, and who in Israel claimed more or less, 1949–1967

claims.text: Lebanon–Israel armistice signed at Ras en Naqoura on 23 March 1949; Article V(1): 'The Armistice Demarcation Line shall follow the international boundary between the Lebanon and Palestine'; withdrawal of forces to the line within ten days (V(3)); Article II(2): no provision shall prejudice the rights, claims and positions of either party
Under the Lebanon agreement Israel withdrew its forces from 13 villages in Lebanese territory occupied during the war

Israel–Syria armistice (S/1353) signed 20 July 1949 near Mahanayim; Art. V(1): line and DMZ arrangements 'are not to be interpreted as having any relation whatsoever to ultimate territorial arrangements'; V(5)(a) DMZ 'from which the armed forces of both Parties shall be totally excluded'; V(2) 'gradual restoration of normal civilian life'
Syria withdrew from most territory it held west of the international border; those areas became demilitarized zones

Sharett called the armistice lines 'provisional boundaries'; at Lausanne 1949 Israel proposed the lines, with minor changes, as the basis for permanent frontiers; the lines enclosed about 78% of Mandate Palestine

18 Nov 1953 Dayan told Byroade and Waller that 'Israel claims sovereignty only over Jewish lands in the Demilitarized Zone' and 'someone must keep the area alive'; Syria wanted the border on the east water line of the Jordan; Israel did not want Syria to have direct access to the river; Byroade said the US 'cannot stand idly by and watch the United Nations machinery fall apart'

Za'im (1949) proposed a summit with Ben-Gurion, a peace agreement and resettlement of 300,000 Palestinians in north-east Syria for US aid; Ben-Gurion refused to meet until Syria withdrew to pre-war positions ('no discussions on peace or cooperation until those borders are adjusted'); Za'im privately told US Minister Keeley he would share Lake Tiberias, giving Israel the western half

Herut was created in June 1948; until the formation of Gahal (1965) it 'maintained that the State of Israel should contain both banks of the River Jordan'; it came fourth in the first Knesset election with 14 seats

Herut was founded by Begin on 15 June 1948; it won 14 seats with 11.5% in 1949, used the slogan 'Two banks of the Jordan River', opposed the ceasefire agreements with the Arab states and refused to recognise the Kingdom of Jordan

Olmert (27 Nov 2006) attributed to Ben-Gurion, in a 1949 Knesset debate on the armistice agreements: faced with the choice between 'the entire land of Israel without a Jewish State' and a Jewish state without it, 'we chose a Jewish State without the entire land of Israel'

Kramer's post quotes Benny Morris that Ben-Gurion in 1948–49 was interested in expanding borders beyond the UN partition lines but 'also refrained from supporting the conquest of the whole Land of Israel'; Kramer notes the declaration of statehood did not specify borders

entries.topic: The 1956 Sinai campaign as a test: Sèvres aims, the 'Third Kingdom' letter, the 7 November Knesset speech, and withdrawal by March 1957

claims.text: The JVL/MFA English text of Ben-Gurion's 7 Nov 1956 Knesset speech does not contain the words 'Third Kingdom', 'kingdom', 'Yotvat' or 'Solomon'; it mentions Tiran ('For centuries this island has been desolate, and only a few years ago the Egyptians occupied and garrisoned it for the purpose of interfering with Israeli shipping in the Gulf')

In the same speech: forces were ordered 'not to cross the Suez Canal or to attack Egyptian territory proper, and remain entirely within the limits of the Sinai Peninsula'; 'the armistice lines between Israel and Egypt have no more validity'; Israel conquered 'the entire Sinai Peninsula of 60,000 square kilometres'; 'Israel wants peace and neighbourly relations with Egypt under conditions of direct negotiations'; the speech does not state whether Israel would withdraw or annex

sources.label: David Ben-Gurion, speech to the Knesset reviewing the Sinai Campaign, 7 November 1956 (Israel MFA text via Jewish Virtual Library); checked 21 Oct 2026 for the 'Third Kingdom' wording
